- **Core Data vs SwiftData contract break**: Codex A's `CaptureSessionModel` draft uses `NSManagedObjectContext` / `WorkoutSession.insert(into:)` (Core Data), but the locked architecture is SwiftData `@Model`/`@ModelActor` ([REDACTED:high_entropy], interfaces.json's `SessionRepository`/`isDemoQueryFilter`). This breaks my `SessionReconciliationService` (`session.persistentModelID`) and anything using `Predicate<WorkoutSession>`. Needs correcting before Milestone 0 can be trusted.
- **RepStateMachine hysteresis bug**: `SquatRuleEngine` wires `enterThreshold: 160, exitThreshold: 100` into `RepStateMachine`, but `update()` checks `measurement >= enterThreshold && measurement <= exitThreshold` — i.e. `>= 160 && <= 100`, an impossible range. As written, no rep will ever register; this blocks the Milestone 1 demo-fixture gate everything else (including my reconciliation/interruption work) depends on being provably real.
- **Lane-ownership overlap**: Codex A (data_domain) drafted `CaptureSessionModel`, `CameraCapabilityDetecting`, and `VisionPoseProcessor` — all owned by primary_ui/services_utilities per DEC-task_assignments-003. Risk of two conflicting implementations landing; integrator should pick one draft and hand finishing to the owning lane.
- **CapturePhase misuse**: Codex A's `guard phase == .readyToRecord` won't compile — `CapturePhase` has associated-value cases and no declared `Equatable`. Also drops the `aligned`/`repCount`/`elapsed`/`exercise` payload the contract requires.
- **My files are SwiftData-only and will break if Core Data ships**: `SessionReconciliationService` and `InterruptionCoordinator` are written strictly against `persistentModelID` / `CapturePhase` pattern-matching per the locked contract — not diverging on my end, but they'll need no changes once data_domain is corrected to SwiftData, and will fail to compile if Core Data stands.
